key_insight: Glymphatic-related measures suggest impaired brain fluid transport in obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), but evidence remains inconclusive for sleep deprivation and narcolepsy type 1.
clinical_relevance: Impaired glymphatic transport may help explain links between OSA, cognitive decline, and neurodegenerative risk, without establishing causation.
method: Systematic review and meta-analysis of clinical and preclinical studies.
Compared glymphatic-related measures across OSA, sleep deprivation, and narcolepsy type 1.
Assessed associations between OSA severity and the DTI-ALPS imaging index.
evidence_signal: Higher apnea-hypopnea index correlated with lower DTI-ALPS index (r = -0.53; 95% CI: -0.63 to -0.41; p < 0.001); no statistically significant alterations were demonstrated for sleep deprivation or narcolepsy type 1.
watch_item: Substantial study heterogeneity and inconsistent methods limit interpretation; nonsignificant findings do not establish normal glymphatic function.
paper_title: Glymphatic Dysfunction Across Sleep Disorders and Its Cognitive Implications
